layers.name: BASE
layers.effect: Global conditioning/control area for Anima diffusion-side inputs: timestep embeddings and the LLM adapter. It controls denoising schedule behavior, prompt/tag interpretation, concept routing, and adapter-to-DiT conditioning. High-impact and fragile: usually keep fixed unless intentionally transferring prompt-understanding or model-wide conditioning behavior. Qwen/text-encoder tensors are not included because they were not present in the provided checkpoint key list.

layers.name: L00
layers.effect: Input/token anchoring stage. Includes x_embedder plus the first DiT block, so it strongly affects latent token formation, coarse local separation, initial edge stability, low-level noise/texture intake, and the earliest image-token structure. Very sensitive for base compatibility.

layers.name: L01
layers.effect: Early structure stage. Establishes simple silhouette, coarse local geometry, early body/clothing mass, and basic prompt-conditioned separation. Useful for subtle structure repair but can affect the base image feel if overused.

layers.name: L02
layers.effect: Early structure/detail stage. Affects local contours, simple limb/body masses, early character placement, and coarse object separation. Good for low-level shape support rather than identity or finished style.

layers.name: L03
layers.effect: Early layout consolidation. Stabilizes broad geometry, person/object separation, camera/layout anchoring, and the transition from coarse latent structure into more semantic layout.

layers.name: L04
layers.effect: Early-mid transformer stage. Begins transferring pose tendencies, clothing structure, body orientation, and prompt-to-structure alignment. Useful for light pose/layout inheritance while still mostly preserving late rendering style.

layers.name: L05
layers.effect: Early-mid structure stage. Useful for body proportions, limb relation, simple interaction geometry, and style-aware shape formation without fully changing the final finish.

layers.name: L06
layers.effect: Early-mid detail routing. Supports clothing complexity, hair/body mass, local structure refinement, and preparation for deeper pose/concept integration.

layers.name: L07
layers.effect: Early-mid pose/detail bridge. Affects dynamic pose individuality, character placement, body orientation, and scene layout before central blocks perform stronger semantic integration.

layers.name: L08
layers.effect: Mid structure stage. Stronger effect on pose coherence, character arrangement, perspective, and prompt-conditioned structure than earlier blocks. Good entry point for pose or scenario transfer.

layers.name: L09
layers.effect: Mid structure and concept stage. Useful for prompt-conditioned body/face relation, multi-part consistency, clothing relation, and early character/scenario binding.

layers.name: L10
layers.effect: Mid integration stage. Balances pose, clothing, face support, identity hints, and concept-conditioned structure. Useful for transferring scenario logic without heavily changing final color.

layers.name: L11
layers.effect: Mid integration bridge. Good for correcting anatomy/layout and prompt-structure alignment while preserving later rendering style. Often safe for structure-focused merges.

layers.name: L12
layers.effect: Central integration stage. Core block for pose, identity hints, body structure, multi-character relation, and global composition mixing. High value for structural or scenario transfer.

layers.name: L13
layers.effect: Central concept/style integration. Affects character identity support, expression support, body/face relationship, scene relation, and global composition. Can start to pull style if MLP is strong.

layers.name: L14
layers.effect: Central detail and structure routing. Useful for clothing/hair detail, hand/body structure, pose consistency, concept stability, and interaction geometry.

layers.name: L15
layers.effect: Central-to-late integration. Bridges structural decisions into local detail and rendering texture. Useful for refined anatomy, expressions, and scenario relation while still carrying broad structure influence.

layers.name: L16
layers.effect: Late-mid structure/rendering bridge. Strong for refined anatomy, hand/finger placement, facial layout, expression, pose stability, and the first visible style/detail formation.

layers.name: L17
layers.effect: Late-mid detail integration. Useful for face/body finish, hand/detail cleanup, clothing density, local consistency, and expression/style balance.

layers.name: L18
layers.effect: Late-mid rendering stage. Impacts lighting, detail clarity, texture, facial/hand finish, and local material separation while still carrying structure influence.

layers.name: L19
layers.effect: Late-mid to late transition. Consolidates local structure, expression, hand/body detail, and style/detail without overhauling early composition as much as later blocks.

layers.name: L20
layers.effect: Late rendering stage. Strong impact on line quality, color response, lighting, texture, and finished style feel. Use cautiously when preserving the base style.

layers.name: L21
layers.effect: Late style/detail stage. Useful for painterly finish, hair/clothing texture, material separation, local polish, and style transfer.

layers.name: L22
layers.effect: Late facial/detail finish. Affects eyes/face finish, local texture, high-level style lock, small detail clarity, and rendering consistency.

layers.name: L23
layers.effect: Late image finish stage. Influences contrast, saturation tendency, detail sharpness, local rendering polish, and final visual density.

layers.name: L24
layers.effect: Very late finish. Strong effect on final color feel, texture, line confidence, small detail reconstruction, and final style lock. Small values can visibly alter output.

layers.name: L25
layers.effect: Very late rendering lock. Useful for final style transfer, lighting/contrast behavior, high-frequency detail, and output polish, but risky for base-style preservation.

layers.name: L26
layers.effect: Very late detail and color lock. Strongly affects output polish, saturation/contrast, final local features, and texture finish. Prefer low strengths unless targeting final look.

layers.name: L27
layers.effect: Final DiT block and output-head area. Strongest late-stage control over final look, color/contrast lock, texture finish, final_layer output behavior, and final latent projection. Very high impact and usually kept low/fixed for structural merges.

layers.name: VAE
layers.effect: VAE encode/decode layers. Empty here because the provided Anima checkpoint element list did not include VAE tensors. Do not assume VAE merge coverage from this candidate map.

elements.name: t_embedder.1.linear_1
elements.effect: Anima timestep embedding first linear stage. Controls denoising-step conditioning, schedule response, global sampling behavior, and how early/late noise states influence structure. High-impact; usually keep low or fixed unless tuning global denoise behavior.

elements.name: t_embedder.1.linear_2
elements.effect: Anima timestep embedding second linear stage. Finishes timestep conditioning and affects global structure/style timing across the denoising trajectory. High-impact; can change model-wide convergence if mixed strongly.

elements.name: t_embedding_norm
elements.effect: Timestep embedding normalization. Stabilizes global denoising balance, prevents unstable or over-sharp timestep conditioning, and affects CFG/sampler response. Fragile global control element.

elements.name: x_embedder.proj.1
elements.effect: Input latent/image-token projection. Controls initial spatial token formation, local separation, low-level structure anchoring, edge/noise intake, and early texture/color foundation. Strong base-compatibility impact.

elements.name: llm_adapter.embed
elements.effect: LLM adapter input embedding. Bridges text/context features into diffusion-side conditioning and affects prompt-adherence foundations, tag vocabulary entry, and concept availability. Very fragile; usually avoid for ordinary style or anatomy merges.

elements.name: llm_adapter.out_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter output projection. Final adapter-to-DiT conditioning output; strongly affects prompt integration strength, tag priority, character/concept routing, and global conditioning behavior. Very high risk if overmixed.

elements.name: llm_adapter.norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter final norm. Balances adapter output scale and conditioning stability before it enters the DiT. Can affect overall prompt strength and concept reliability.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.q_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention query. Determines what text/context relations the adapter attends to, including tag ordering, character-attribute binding, and natural-language relation interpretation.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.k_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention key. Controls adapter-side context matching and lookup for text tokens/concepts. Affects how reliably related tags or phrases are associated.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.v_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention value. Carries adapter-side context feature content, including concept and relation information that can later affect image conditioning.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.o_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention output. Integrates adapter-side context mixing and text relation interpretation; can alter prompt parsing behavior globally.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.q_norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention q norm. Stabilizes adapter token-relation queries and helps prevent over/under-attention to text-token relations.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.k_norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention k norm. Stabilizes adapter matching scale and text-context lookup behavior.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.q_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention query. Routes prompt-conditioned context inside the adapter and affects how external/context features are requested by adapter tokens.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.k_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention key. Controls external context lookup and prompt matching inside the adapter. Important for tag/concept availability and relation matching.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.v_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention value. Injects external context/style/concept content into the adapter representation. Strongly tied to prompt and concept transfer.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.o_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention output. Finishes prompt/context integration inside the adapter and can alter final prompt-conditioning behavior.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.q_norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention q norm. Stabilizes prompt-routing queries and balanced conditioning strength in adapter cross attention.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.k_norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention k norm. Stabilizes context lookup and prompt matching scale in adapter cross attention.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.mlp.0
elements.effect: LLM adapter MLP first projection. Expands adapter features and transforms text/concept representations; can carry character, style, and relation knowledge. High-risk for broad prompt behavior.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.mlp.2
elements.effect: LLM adapter MLP output projection. Compresses adapter features and finishes conditioning representation; affects concept priority and final adapter semantics.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.norm_self_attn
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention norm. Stabilizes self-context processing around adapter self attention and affects text-token relation balance.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.norm_cross_attn
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention norm. Balances prompt/context features before or around adapter cross attention; affects concept routing stability.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.norm_mlp
elements.effect: LLM adapter MLP norm. Balances adapter feature transformation and conditioning stability before/around concept MLP processing.

elements.name: self_attn.q_proj
elements.effect: DiT self-attention query. Decides what image-token relations to attend to; strongly affects pose/layout consistency, body-part relation, multi-character separation, and spatial reasoning.

elements.name: self_attn.k_proj
elements.effect: DiT self-attention key. Provides image-token structural matching and spatial lookup; affects how body parts, characters, and objects correspond across the image.

elements.name: self_attn.v_proj
elements.effect: DiT self-attention value. Carries internal image feature content through self attention, including structure material, local detail, and pose/anatomy information.

elements.name: self_attn.output_proj
elements.effect: DiT self-attention output. Integrates self-attention results into the block output; controls structural finish, global consistency, pose cohesion, and multi-part image stability.

elements.name: self_attn.q_norm
elements.effect: DiT self-attention q norm. Stabilizes query strength in self attention and helps control structural balance, anatomy drift, and excessive image-token attention.

elements.name: self_attn.k_norm
elements.effect: DiT self-attention k norm. Stabilizes self-attention matching and helps prevent unstable structure drift, duplicate parts, or weak spatial correspondence.

elements.name: cross_attn.q_proj
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention query. Determines how image tokens request prompt/context information; affects prompt adherence, character/object placement, scenario binding, and tag-controlled structure.

elements.name: cross_attn.k_proj
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention key. Controls text/context lookup and matching for characters, objects, relationships, style tags, and attribute binding.

elements.name: cross_attn.v_proj
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention value. Injects concept/style/content from conditioning into image tokens; affects character traits, clothing, expression cues, object details, and style content.

elements.name: cross_attn.output_proj
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention output. Integrates prompt/context information into the image stream; affects final prompt adherence, concept finish, style transfer, and scenario coherence.

elements.name: cross_attn.q_norm
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention q norm. Stabilizes prompt-routing strength from image tokens and helps balance under/over-adherence to conditioning.

elements.name: cross_attn.k_norm
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention k norm. Stabilizes context lookup and prompt matching scale; useful for reducing unstable tag mixing or weak concept binding.

elements.name: mlp.layer1
elements.effect: DiT MLP first projection. Expands per-token features; affects drawing density, shape refinement, face/hand/clothing detail, material texture, and style/detail formation.

elements.name: mlp.layer2
elements.effect: DiT MLP second projection. Compresses and returns transformed features; affects detail finish, rendering consolidation, local polish, style output, and color/texture expression.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_self_attn.1
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for self-attention first stage. Timestep/conditioning modulation over internal structure and pose; affects how strongly self-attention participates at each denoise phase.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_self_attn.2
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for self-attention second stage. Self-attention gating and denoising-step balance; useful for controlling pose/anatomy influence without directly replacing attention weights.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_cross_attn.1
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for cross-attention first stage. Timestep/conditioning modulation over prompt-conditioning strength and concept routing balance.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_cross_attn.2
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for cross-attention second stage. Cross-attention gating and prompt/style influence; affects how strongly prompt concepts enter image tokens across denoising.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_mlp.1
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for MLP first stage. Controls feature expansion balance for density, lighting, material expression, and style/detail growth over denoising.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_mlp.2
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for MLP second stage. MLP gating and rendering finish; affects style/detail strength, polish, and late-stage texture consolidation.

elements.name: final_layer.adaln_modulation.1
elements.effect: Final-layer AdaLN modulation first stage. Final denoising/output conditioning and image-head balance; affects output-head response, color/contrast tendency, and final structural projection.

elements.name: final_layer.adaln_modulation.2
elements.effect: Final-layer AdaLN modulation second stage. Final output gating and last-stage image look lock; high-impact for final style/color/detail behavior.

elements.name: final_layer.linear
elements.effect: Final linear image head. Final latent-to-output projection; strongly affects final color/contrast lock, texture finish, output sharpness, and visible image structure. Very sensitive.

mode_notes.Checkpoint: Use these as guidance when designing Anima checkpoint merge elemental ratios. For SIM/AD-style merges, use alpha mainly as difference-injection amount and beta as a similarity/stability gate. L00-L07 bias input/early structure and coarse layout; L08-L15 are the safest core range for pose, scenario relation, prompt-structure binding, and multi-character composition; L16-L19 refine face, expression, hands, anatomy, clothing, and local structure; L20-L27 strongly influence final rendering, style, color, lighting, contrast, and detail lock. BASE/llm_adapter, t_embedder, x_embedder, and final_layer are high-impact global areas and should usually be fixed or used at very low strength unless intentionally changing conditioning or output-head behavior.
mode_notes.LoRA: For Anima LoRA bake, use narrow attention/MLP/AdaLN targets when preserving the base. self_attn is best for pose, layout, anatomy, and multi-character separation; cross_attn is best for prompt adherence, characters, clothing, objects, and scenario concepts; mlp is best for face/hand/clothing detail, texture, rendering density, color, and style; AdaLN modulation changes when/how strongly those paths act during denoising. Avoid or minimize llm_adapter unless the LoRA intentionally trains prompt-understanding/knowledge behavior. Late L20-L27 and final_layer targets strongly affect finish and color.
mode_notes.LyCORIS: LyCORIS can target the same logical elements. Per-layer validity matters: BASE contains timestep and adapter elements, L00-L27 contain DiT block elements, L00 additionally has x_embedder, and L27 additionally has final_layer elements. For base preservation, prefer central self_attn/cross_attn/AdaLN subsets over broad all-layer MLP or final_layer targeting. For style transfer, prefer L16-L27 MLP/AdaLN_MLP with cautious late-block strength.
